title: Roth withdrawal order: contributions, conversions, earnings
audience: Anyone with a multi-year Roth who thinks all withdrawals are tax-free
thesis: Roth withdrawals come out in a fixed order — and the order matters for the 5-year rule and the 10% penalty.

concepts.label: The ordering rule
concepts.body: Roth IRA withdrawals follow a fixed order: regular contributions come out first, then conversions on a first-in-first-out basis, then earnings last. The IRS treats the buckets separately (IRC §408A(d)(4)).

concepts.label: Why the order matters
concepts.body: If you withdraw $20,000 from a Roth that holds $15,000 contributions and $5,000 earnings, the first $15,000 is always tax-and-penalty-free. The next $5,000 is earnings — which can trigger the 10% penalty if you're under 59½ and no exception applies.

concepts.label: Conversions have their own 5-year clock
concepts.body: Each Roth conversion starts its own 5-year clock for the 10% penalty. Convert in 2023, withdraw converted amount in 2025 — that's under 5 years, 10% penalty applies unless an age-based exception kicks in.

sources: IRC §408A(d)(4) — ordering rules for Roth distributions
IRS Pub 590-B — Distributions from Individual Retirement Arrangements
IRS Form 8606 instructions — non-deductible IRA / Roth conversion tracking
